findings.question: are flagged bodies wrong more often than chance would give?
does the audit ever flag a correct answer? (it must not)
findings.why_it_matters: a false alarm triggers attribution against an innocent concept, which is the exact failure the attribution round fixed

findings.conclusion: a well-formed, total, balanced body that is simply false is invisible
findings.question: can a body be wrong with NO observable structural defect?
does the audit see the answer it is auditing?

not_claimed: that the audit detects wrong answers -- it detects DEFECTS, and only 9 of 10 wrong answers had one in this sample
that recall 0.90 generalises; the sample is 20 synthesized bodies over one corpus
that a clean verdict means correct -- it means nothing was visibly wrong, which is a different and much weaker statement
that this is a judgement about when to spend effort; the benchmark treats every flagged body as worth auditing
